Description

Power that runs the world | Discover careers in Operations

Operations roles at Amazon put you at the center of how things move from a click to a doorstep. You'll help design, improve, and run systems that connect people, products, and places at scale. You'll take ownership early, work closely with teams to solve real-world challenges, and see the direct results of your decisions as they reach customers every day. Here, the impact of what you build isn't abstract, it's visible, immediate, and meaningful - keeping one of the world's most complex operations moving forward. This is where your journey takes shape through action, responsibility, and the opportunity to grow in many directions.

IMPORTANT NOTE: This role is based out of our corporate office in Bellevue, WA. Applicants must be able to work on-site at our Bellevue, WA office during the spring semester and be available for travel during summer months. During summer months, travel to Amazon fulfillment centers under construction and corporate offices around the US is required.

The Business Strategy & Execution Operations Engineering Internship is an on-site part-time internship (20 hours a week) during the Spring 2027 academic season (February 2027 - May/June 2027) based in our Bellevue, WA corporate office.

Upon school release for Summer 2026 (May/June 2027 - July/August 2027) this position shifts to a 12-week internship "full-time" (40 hours/week) with travel opportunities to fulfillment centers under construction and corporate offices across the United States.

This is a hybrid corporate and field position, combining strategic business work in our corporate office environment with hands-on operations engineering support at fulfillment centers, sort centers, delivery stations, and construction/job trailer environments.

Amazon is searching for innovative and solutions-oriented Business Strategy & Execution Operations Engineering Interns to be a part of our North America initiative to develop and deliver next generation, world-class fulfillment systems while building strategic frameworks that drive operational excellence. What is fulfillment you ask? Fulfillment is how we refer to completing or fulfilling a customer's Amazon.com order and the acts of picking, packing, shipping, sorting and delivering their order to meet or exceed their expectations!

Our Business Strategy & Execution Operations Engineers have the ability to quickly strategize, plan and execute solutions to complex business challenges while building scalable mechanisms that drive standardization, operational efficiency and organizational success. They are comfortable in ambiguous, fast-moving environments, using strategic insight and influence to align cross-functional teams and drive coordinated execution across the network. Guided by curiosity, customer obsession, and innovation, they transform ideas into mechanisms that enable NA Operations Engineering’s most advanced business operations.

Key job responsibilities
Drive resolution for strategic business projects by owning and deep diving data to support process improvement recommendations and organizational frameworks.

Build standard operating procedures for teams to follow, ensuring scalable and repeatable business processes.

Develop business plans that help the organization run more smoothly and efficiently during peak operational periods

Support Operations Engineers in the field manage, test and implement integrated automation projects with elements such as high-speed sortation, multiple conveyors, package lines, and/or robotic work cells

Guide and coordinate design and execution efforts between internal teams and outside vendors including equipment specifications, material flow, process design, and site layout

Coordinate with local site management to ensure proper operator training, procedural compliance, maintenance and safety practices are followed for new and existing equipment

Manage and streamline administrative operations support, including project tracking systems coordination, documentation management, and identifying opportunities to automate routine administrative processes to improve operational efficiency

A day in the life
Work 12-hour shifts on feet (when supporting field operations)

Cover extensive distances in large warehouse facilities

Use ladders, stairs, and gangways safely
Lift/move totes up to 49 lbs

Perform frequent bending, stretching, and reaching motions

Travel to various locations across the United States during summer months

- Are 18 years of age or older
- Currently enrolled in a bachelor’s degree program with all requirements anticipated to be completed between December 2027 and August 2028.
- Able to work on-site at Amazon's Bellevue, WA corporate office
- Available to work part-time (20 hours/week) during Spring 2026 semester (February 2027 - May/June 2027) from our Bellevue, WA office
- Available to transition to full-time (40 hours/week) for a 12-week period during Summer 2027 (May/June 2027 - July/August 2027)
- Able to travel up to 80% to fulfillment centers under construction and corporate offices across the United States during summer months

- Experience with standard work development and process documentation

Backed by hundreds of millions from top-tier investors and staffed by leading engineers, we're redefining the infrastructure layer for the fastest growing industry in history.

Job Summary
Core Engineering is our special projects team. This team identifies critical gaps across Etched and builds solutions 0 to 1, often in days, with immediate feedback loops. You might build internal tools to unblock a hardware team, prototype systems for manufacturing execution, or design, evaluate, and deploy agentic systems for our most challenging R&D problems.

This role is for engineers who thrive on ambiguity, move fast without sacrificing quality, and get energy from solving whatever problem matters most right now. It is a whiteboard for future founders – if you're interested in shipping 0-1 production-level code every week, this role is for you.

This role requires exceptional full-stack engineering capabilities, deep product sense, personal accountability, and a knack for building from the ground up. At Etched, we're developing our processes for scale, and we're looking for engineers to deploy to our toughest challenges. The problems we solve are time-sensitive and business-critical. This role will not be a 9-5, and the ideal candidate is excited about that. This is not a shadowing program. You will own a real project, scoped to land in production and shape how Etched executes.

You may be a good fit if you:

- Have a track record of solving hard problems across stacks and domains — you enjoy being dropped into unfamiliar territory and figuring it out

- Have something you built that you can walk us through in depth. Depth in one thing beats a list of ten

- Are comfortable with Python and TypeScript: you can read it, modify it, debug it, and direct AI to write it well. We don't care whether you write code from scratch, but we do care whether you ship things that work

- Have product sense and its necessary prerequisites, from AI tooling proficiency to design taste

- Bias towards action and comfort with incomplete information

- Data engineering, infrastructure or DevOps experience, and deploying operational systems in enterprise environments

- Experience wielding frontier models on frontier problems: an eval-driven mindset — you measure whether AI systems work, identify where they fall short, and know how to hillclimb

- High agency and comfort with ambiguity — you find the real problem to solve

- Prior startup experience, especially during hyper growth

- 12-week paid internship (June - August 2026)

- Generous housing support for those relocating

- Daily lunch and dinner in our office

- Based at our office in San Jose, CA

- Direct mentorship from industry leaders and world-class engineers

- Opportunity to work on one of the most important problems of our time

For any questions, contact internships@etched.com

How we're different
Etched believes in the Bitter Lesson. We are the first inference-focused frontier AI system, betting early on transformer and transformer-like architectures and on increasing model sizes. Our addressable market is the entirety of inference.

We are a fully in-person team in San Jose and Taipei, and greatly value engineering skills. We do not have boundaries between engineering and research, and we expect all of our technical staff to contribute to both and work across disciplines as needed.

We are seeking highly motivated, technically exceptional interns to join our team in the rapidly growing field of Vehicle Health Management (VHM). If you have a passion for applying autonomous driving technologies to impact the flow of goods for millions of people, we want to talk to you!

Job Description

We’re looking for Autonomy Engineering interns who are eager to bring autonomous driving systems to life from the ground up. Minimum internship duration is 4 months, with direct conversion to full-time available.

Specifically, we are looking for individuals who have deep functional expertise in one or more of the following areas:

- Perception and Sensor Fusion
- Localization and Mapping
- Vehicle Control, Planning, and Decision Making

- Work with the engineering team at large to support all aspects of ground vehicle autonomy, including planning, perception, navigation, and infrastructure subsystems

- Collaborate with hardware engineering to create an integrated system, including calibration and integration

- Understand and keep up-to-date with state of the art

- Background in developing the autonomy (sensing, decision-making, or control) functions of a deployed, autonomous vehicle

- Experience shipping a working robotics or vehicle autonomy subsystem

- Candidates with unconventional experiences especially encouraged

- Willingness to get hands-on and have lots of fun

About ProFound Therapeutics

ProFound™ Therapeutics is a biotechnology company discovering novel proteins across the expanded human proteome to unlock first-in-class medicines and transformative drug targets. Founded by Flagship Pioneering, ProFound works with pharmaceutical partners including Novartis, Pfizer and GSK, and with the Gates Foundation, which has committed up to $35 million to a ProFoundprogram focused on preeclampsia.

ProFound Therapeutics was founded by Flagship Pioneering's venture creation engine that invents and builds platform companies, each with the potential for multiple products that transform human health or sustainability. Since its launch in 2000, Flagship has originated and fostered more than 100 scientific ventures, resulting in more than $90 billion in aggregate value. Welcome to Flagship Pioneering Co-Op Program for the cohort dreaming big and taking courageous leaps. Position Summary

As a Bioinformatics Data Engineering Co-Op, you’ll work on production pipelines and datasets, with code review and mentorship from the team. You’ll own a scoped project from start to finish and present it to the team at the end. Typical projects include a QC dashboard, a pipeline benchmark, a new annotation resource or a statistics module. You’ll also work directly with the scientists who use what you build.

The Co-Op is designed to complement your academic training with hands-on experience in production bioinformatics and data engineering in an industry drug discovery setting.

Key Responsibilities

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following.

- Run and monitor pipelines. Run Nextflow pipelines for ribosome profiling (Ribo-seq), long-read sequencing and DIA proteomics on AWS Batch. Triage failed jobs and summarize QC with MultiQC and alignment metrics.

- Build and validate QC. Flag samples that fail set thresholds. Compare results across GENCODE versions. Write automated checks that catch suspicious or missing experiment data before it reaches downstream scoring.

- Analyze proteomics evidence. This includes peptide-to-protein mapping, sequence coverage, FDR-filtered evidence, and comparisons across search engines and experiments.

- Write and test scripts. Use Python and R to parse, filter and summarize outputs (FASTA, GTF, BAM, peptide and protein tables) into Parquet or TSV. Turn exploratory notebooks into reusable, version-controlled code.

- Grow the data catalog. Add or update a dataset: ingest it, document its schema and check it with Athena (SQL) queries.

- Build tools for scientists. Prototype a visualization or dashboard (Plotly/Dash, Streamlit or a notebook) that scientists use to review targets and QC results.

- Document and share. Write READMEs and runbooks, and present results in team meetings, including a final co-op presentation.

Example Projects

- Benchmark two MS search engines on the same dataset and report where they agree and where they disagree.

- Build a Ribo-seq QC report that flags samples failing periodicity or mapping thresholds.

- Add a new QC view to a scientist-facing dashboard, from requirements through deployment.

- Ingest and document a new biological annotation resource in the data catalog.

Qualifications

Required

- Currently pursuing a B.S. or M.S. in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Biology, Biochemistry, Computer Science or a related field, and available for a full-time, 4–6 month co-op term.

- Python (pandas) and comfort with the Linux command line.

- Git, and a habit of writing clear, tested, reproducible code.

- Coursework or project experience in genomics or molecular biology, such as RNA-seq, translation, protein or DNA sequence analysis, or proteomics basics.

- Clear written communication; you document what you build.

Preferred

- Basic R.

- SQL.

- Nextflow, Snakemake, Airflow or another workflow manager, plus Docker.

- Exposure to AWS (e.g., S3, EC2, Athena).

- Familiarity with Ribo-seq, long-read sequencing or mass spectrometry data (e.g., peptides, PSMs, database search).

- Basic statistics, such as differential expression, false discovery rate and multiple-testing correction.

- A dashboard or web app you’ve built (e.g., Dash, Streamlit, Shiny), linked from GitHub or a portfolio.

- Experience with AI coding assistants (e.g., Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor) on real projects, with a sense of where they help and where they fail.

- Exposure to LLM APIs, agents, MCP, or classic ML (e.g., scikit-learn, PyTorch) applied to biological data.

What You’ll Learn and Gain

- How production Nextflow pipelines are built, tested and run on the cloud.

- How a data catalog (Glue, Athena, Parquet) turns raw omics outputs into queryable resources.

- How a computational team supports a drug discovery platform, with exposure to the wet-lab work behind the data.

- How to use AI-assisted development responsibly in a regulated, data-sensitive setting: verification, testing, and knowing what data may and may not go to which tools.

- A shipped project with your name on it.

What We Offer

- Build alongside founders. You’ll work inside the same hypothesis-driven process Flagship uses to conceive and launch first-in-category companies.

- This can be the start of a longer story. Strong co-ops are considered for future opportunities across Flagship and its portfolio companies, not just for this one role.

- Work alongside people who left the safe path. Your colleagues are scientists, engineers, and operators who chose to build something new rather than join something already established.
